answer: A randomized committee drawn by age rather than capital stops clone farms from voting themselves into power. Each epoch the protocol samples graders from identities with long attested histories, so new keys queue at the back and a fresh cluster's weight dilutes on arrival. Every verdict must carry a checksum recomputed from the public beacon, so one script cannot batch copied votes. A thousand yarrow seeds dropped into a canyon do not become a forest: they sprout yet weigh nothing until seasons pass, while a single juniper already rooted holds the slope. Clones pay full upkeep for no voice.
